examples.en: We climbed the mountain in extreme cold.
The athlete pushed his body to the limit.
My patience reached its limit.
He acted calmly even in an extreme situation.
It was a challenge that went beyond the limit.
He crossed the desert fighting against the extremes.

explain: '한계'는 넘기 어려운 선이고, '극한'은 그 선에 거의 닿은 가장 심한 상태예요. '극한의 추위', '극한 직업'처럼 어려움이 아주 클 때 붙여요. 수학에서는 다른 뜻의 용어로도 나와요.
explain_en: '한계' is a line that is hard to cross, while 극한 is the most severe state, almost at that line. It is attached as in '극한의 추위' (extreme cold) or '극한 직업' (an extremely tough job). In math it is also a term with a different meaning.

examples.en: Our cat is really quick.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 몸이 날래서 상대가 잡지 못해요.
examples.en: That player is so nimble that opponents can't catch him.
He caught the ball with a swift move.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 다람쥐처럼 날래게 나무를 탔어요.
examples.en: The child climbed the tree swiftly like a squirrel.
If your hands are quick, cooking finishes fast too.

examples.ko: 날래지 못한 저는 항상 늦게 도착해요.
examples.en: I'm not quick, so I always arrive late.

explain: '빠르다'가 속도 전반을 말한다면 '날래다'는 몸이나 손의 움직임이 재빠르다는 느낌이에요. 대화에서는 '빠르다', '재빠르다'를 쓰기도 하고, 불규칙 없이 '날래요', '날랜'으로 활용해요.
explain_en: While '빠르다' covers speed in general, '날래다' feels like quick movement of the body or hands. In conversation people may also say '빠르다' or '재빠르다', and it conjugates regularly: '날래요', '날랜'.

examples.ko: 저 고양이는 정말 날쌔서 잡을 수가 없어요.
examples.en: That cat is so quick that I can't catch it.
That player's body is very nimble.
A nimble squirrel climbed up the tree.
My younger brother ran over swiftly and caught the ball.
I'm not fast on my feet, but I run to the end.
A kid who looked nimble ran out first.

explain: '빠르다'는 속도 전반에 쓰지만 '날쌔다'는 사람이나 동물의 몸놀림이 재빠르고 가벼울 때 써요. 그래서 자동차나 인터넷 속도에는 '날쌔다'를 쓰지 않아요. 반대 느낌은 '굼뜨다'이고, 비슷한 말로 '날래다'도 있어요.
explain_en: '빠르다' (fast) works for speed in general, but '날쌔다' is for the quick, light movements of a person or animal. So you don't use it for cars or internet speed. The opposite feeling is '굼뜨다' (slow, sluggish), and '날래다' is a similar word.

examples.en: He honestly admitted his own incompetence.
I was so ashamed of my own incompetence that I cried.

examples.ko: 상사의 무능력 때문에 팀 전체가 고생했어요.
examples.en: The whole team suffered because of the boss's incompetence.
That politician was criticized for incompetence.
Faced with repeated failures, I felt incompetent.

examples.ko: 무능력은 아니고 단지 경험이 부족할 뿐이에요.
examples.en: It's not incompetence, just a lack of experience.

explain: '능력이 없다'보다 딱딱하고 평가하는 느낌이 강해서, 사람을 향해 쓰면 꽤 심한 비난으로 들려요. 비슷한 '무능'도 있고, 부드럽게 말할 때는 '능력이 부족하다'라고 해요. 자기 자신에 대해 말할 때 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is stiffer and more judgmental than '능력이 없다', so aimed at a person it can sound like harsh criticism. There is also the similar '무능', and a softer way to say it is '능력이 부족하다'. It is often used when talking about oneself.

examples.en: The color of the outfit and the shoes clash.
In this room the furniture and wallpaper don't go together.
A mismatch between words and actions lowers trust.

examples.ko: 새 건물이 주변 마을과 부조화를 보여서 말이 많아요.
examples.en: The new building looks out of place next to the village, so people are talking.
The music and the video clashed, so it felt awkward.
Even in the mismatch, there is a certain charm.

explain: '조화'의 반대말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '안 어울리다'가 더 자연스럽고, '부조화'는 글이나 설명에서 많이 써요. 색이나 모양뿐 아니라 말과 행동이 맞지 않을 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of '조화' (harmony). In daily talk '안 어울리다' sounds more natural, while '부조화' is common in writing and explanations. It covers not only colors and shapes but also words and actions that don't match.

examples.en: The glass fell on the floor and shattered into pieces.

examples.ko: 시험에 떨어져서 내 계획이 산산조각 났어요.
examples.en: I failed the exam, and my plans were shattered.

examples.ko: 화가 나서 편지를 산산조각 찢어 버렸어요.
examples.en: I got angry and tore the letter into tiny pieces.
The window smashed into pieces from the impact.

examples.ko: 산산조각 난 도자기를 다시 붙이는 데 한 달이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a month to glue the shattered pottery back together.

examples.ko: 아이가 장난감 로봇을 산산조각으로 부숴 놓았어요.
examples.en: The child smashed the toy robot to bits.

explain: '산산조각이 나다', '산산조각 내다'처럼 말하고, 물건이 여러 조각으로 깨질 때 써요. 꿈, 계획, 희망, 믿음처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것이 완전히 무너질 때도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is used as '산산조각이 나다' or '산산조각 내다' for things breaking into many pieces. It is also common for intangible things such as dreams, plans, hopes and trust being completely destroyed.

examples.ko: 사장님이 오늘은 선심 써서 음료수를 공짜로 줬어요.
examples.en: The owner was generous today and gave us drinks for free.

examples.ko: 선심 쓰듯 말하지 말고 진심으로 도와주세요.
examples.en: Don't talk as if you're doing me a big favor; help me sincerely.

examples.ko: 선거 때가 되면 선심성 공약이 쏟아져요.
examples.en: When election time comes, handout-style pledges pour out.

examples.ko: 큰맘 먹고 선심 한번 쓸게요. 오늘 커피는 제가 살게요.
examples.en: I'll be generous for once. The coffee is on me today.
Please don't act like you're being so generous.

examples.ko: 선심을 쓸 형편이 아닌데도 친구에게 밥을 샀어요.
examples.en: I wasn't in a position to be generous, but I bought my friend a meal anyway.

explain: 거의 '선심(을) 쓰다'로 나와서, 남에게 후하게 베푸는 모습을 말해요. 때로는 생색내는 느낌이 있고, '선심성 공약'처럼 정치 이야기에서는 비판하는 말로 자주 써요.
explain_en: It almost always appears as '선심(을) 쓰다', meaning to give generously to others. It can carry a hint of showing off, and in politics, as in '선심성 공약' (handout-style pledges), it is often used critically.

examples.en: This movie is really big in scale.
I was amazed by the scale of the concert hall.
The budget was short, so we cut back the scale of the event.
That person is generous and thinks on another scale.
Stories about space are different in scale from the start.
It's a small shop, but the scale of the ideas is big.

explain: 스케일은 영어 scale에서 온 말이지만 한국어에서는 '규모가 크다', '통이 크다'는 칭찬으로 자주 써요. '스케일이 크다'가 가장 흔하고, 작다고 말할 때는 '규모가 작다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: 스케일 comes from English 'scale', but in Korean it is often used as praise meaning big in size or generous in spirit. 스케일이 크다 is the most common pattern; to say something is small, people more often say 규모가 작다.

examples.ko: 악조건 속에서도 선수들은 끝까지 최선을 다했어요.
examples.en: Even under bad conditions, the players did their best to the end.
We overcame the bad conditions of rain and wind.
Bad conditions piled up, and the construction was delayed a lot.
It is dangerous to drive in conditions like these.
Despite the bad conditions, we finished the match safely.
We canceled the hike because of several unfavorable conditions.

explain: 날씨, 환경, 형편이 좋지 않아 일하기 힘든 상황을 말해요. 반대말은 '호조건'이고, 일상에서는 '좋은 조건'이라고도 많이 말해요. '악조건 속에서', '악조건을 이기다', '악조건을 극복하다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It describes poor circumstances, such as weather, environment or situation, that make things hard. The opposite is '호조건', and in daily talk people also just say '좋은 조건'. Common patterns are '악조건 속에서', '악조건을 이기다' and '악조건을 극복하다'.

examples.en: No matter how much I persuade him, he won't budge.
The negotiation dragged on because of his immovable attitude.
He sat there motionless like a rock.
The player who held firm without budging looked cool.

examples.ko: 요지부동일 줄 알았는데 결국 마음을 바꿨어요.
examples.en: I thought he'd never budge, but he finally changed his mind.

examples.ko: 상대가 요지부동이라서 대화가 전혀 안 돼요.
examples.en: The other side won't budge, so we can't talk at all.

explain: '요지부동이다' 꼴로 많이 쓰고, 몸이 움직이지 않는 모습과 마음이나 태도가 바뀌지 않는 모습에 모두 써요. 사람의 고집을 말할 때는 칭찬보다 답답하다는 느낌이 더 자주 담겨요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '요지부동이다' and covers both a body that doesn't move and an attitude or mind that doesn't change. When describing a person's stubbornness it more often carries frustration than praise.

examples.en: That player's talent is one of a kind.

examples.ko: 유일무이한 존재가 되고 싶어서 열심히 노력해요.
examples.en: I work hard because I want to become one and only.

examples.ko: 이 방법이 유일무이하지는 않지만 꽤 효과가 있어요.
examples.en: This method isn't the one and only, but it works quite well.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 목소리는 유일무이해서 금방 알아들을 수 있어요.
examples.en: That singer's voice is one of a kind, so you can recognize it right away.
At that time, this technology was the only one of its kind in Korea.
It was such a special experience that you could call it one of a kind.

explain: '유일하다'는 단순히 하나뿐이라는 말이고, '유일무이하다'는 둘도 없이 특별하다는 강조의 느낌이 있어요. 조금 딱딱해서 칭찬하거나 소개하는 글에서 잘 보여요.
explain_en: '유일하다' simply means there is only one, while '유일무이하다' adds emphasis that nothing else compares. It is a bit formal and shows up in praise or introductions.

examples.ko: 그 아이의 손은 작디작아서 정말 귀여웠어요.
examples.en: The child's hands were tiny and so cute.
A big tree grows from a tiny seed.

examples.ko: 이 인형 신발은 아기 손가락만큼 작디작아요.
examples.en: These doll shoes are tiny, about the size of a baby's finger.
The tiny puppy has already grown this big.

examples.ko: 글씨가 작디작아도 저는 잘 읽을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even if the writing is tiny, I can read it well.
People who look tiny are walking outside the window.

explain: '작다'에 '-디'를 넣어 같은 말을 되풀이해 '아주 작다'를 강조하는 말이에요. '크디크다', '높디높다'처럼 반대되는 뜻의 말도 같은 방식으로 만들어요. 일상 대화보다는 글이나 이야기에서 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It repeats '작다' with '-디' in the middle to stress 'very small'. Words like '크디크다' and '높디높다' are built the same way for the opposite meanings. It appears more in writing and storytelling than in casual talk.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 어려울 때마다 놀라운 저력을 보여 줘요.
examples.en: That team shows amazing hidden strength every time things get hard.
They say the underlying strength of the Korean economy is great.
A new singer with real potential has appeared.

examples.ko: 그 팀이 보여 준 저력에 모두 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Everyone was surprised by the strength that team showed.
We still have some strength left in us.
Many shops got through it on their underlying strength.

explain: 평소에는 잘 안 보이다가 어려운 때에 드러나는 숨은 힘을 말해요. 그냥 '힘'이나 '능력'과 달리 팀, 회사, 나라처럼 밑바탕이 있는 대상에 잘 어울려요. '저력을 보이다', '저력을 발휘하다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It refers to hidden strength that is not obvious usually but shows when times are hard. Unlike plain '힘' or '능력', it suits things with a solid foundation, like a team, company or country. Common patterns are '저력을 보이다' and '저력을 발휘하다'.

examples.en: My mom's cooking skill is something special.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 고집이 특별나서 말을 잘 안 들어요.
examples.en: That child is unusually stubborn, so he doesn't listen well.
There's no particular reason for it.
My town is known for being exceptionally warm-hearted.
Grandfather's love for his grandchildren is exceptional.
There's no need to act so peculiar.

explain: 다른 것과 비교해서 눈에 띄게 다르거나 유난하다는 느낌이에요. '특별하다'보다 구어체이고, 때로는 좀 유난스럽다는 뉘앙스도 있어요. '특별난 이유가 없다'처럼 부정문에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It carries the feel of being noticeably different or out of the ordinary. It is more colloquial than '특별하다' and sometimes has a nuance of being a bit over the top. It often appears in negatives like '특별난 이유가 없다'.

examples.en: Being short is a handicap in basketball.
I think my Korean pronunciation is a handicap.
In golf, skill differences are balanced with a handicap.
I practiced every day to overcome that handicap.

examples.ko: 경험이 없는 건 큰 핸디캡이 아니에요.
examples.en: Having no experience is not a big disadvantage.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 핸디캡을 안고 시합을 시작했어요.
examples.en: Our team started the match with a handicap.

explain: 핸디캡은 '불리한 조건'이라는 뜻으로는 '약점'이나 '불리한 점'과 비슷해요. 몸이 불편한 사람을 가리킬 때는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요. 골프나 바둑에서는 실력 차이를 맞추는 규칙으로도 써요.
explain_en: 핸디캡 as a disadvantage is close to '약점' or '불리한 점'. It is better not to use it to describe a person with a disability. In golf and baduk it also means a rule that evens out skill differences.
